record.paper_title: NTN-based 6G Localization: Vision, Role of LEOs, and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Doppler-based FDOA support in cellular NTN positioning
record.original_question: How can non-terrestrial-network (NTN) positioning make Doppler-based frequency-difference-of-arrival (FDOA) practical in a 5G or 6G cellular framework when current 5G positioning signaling supports delay-based methods but not Doppler-based methods, accurate three-dimensional FDOA may require at least eight visible low-earth-orbit (LEO) satellites, and the existing positioning reference signal (PRS) would need redesign to deliver sufficient Doppler resolution?

evidence.quote: Note that 5G positioning has the capability and signaling support to accommodate most of the delay-based positioning methods but not any Doppler-based positioning methods such as FDOA.

Although FDOA has been considered for LEO-based positioning, e.g., see [3], its implementation poses several challenges. First, it requires at least 8 visible LEOs to perform accurate 3D estimation which is not always guaranteed. Second, the need for a significant redesign of the existing PRS to provide sufficient Doppler resolution for accurate FDOA measurements.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a cellular positioning framework (5G/6G) in which a user equipment (UE) on or near the Earth's surface receives downlink positioning reference signals (PRS) from a constellation of low-earth-orbit (LEO) satellites. Each satellite i has known time-varying position p_i(t) ∈ ℝ^3 and velocity v_i(t) ∈ ℝ^3, and transmits a carrier of nominal frequency f_c. The UE has unknown 3D position x ∈ ℝ^3, unknown clock bias b ∈ ℝ, and unknown carrier frequency offset δ ∈ ℝ. From the received signal of satellite i the UE can in principle measure the instantaneous Doppler shift
   f_i = -(f_c / c) · ⟨v_i − ẋ, (x − p_i)/‖x − p_i‖⟩ + δ + n_i,
where c is the speed of light and n_i is measurement noise. By forming frequency differences f_i − f_j (frequency-difference-of-arrival, FDOA) the unknown δ is eliminated, leaving a system of nonlinear equations in x (and possibly ẋ).

Known facts to be taken as given:
(i) Current cellular positioning signaling supports delay-/time-based observables (e.g., TDOA) but does not natively support Doppler-based observables such as FDOA.
(ii) Accurate 3D position estimation by FDOA alone is generally ill-conditioned unless at least 8 LEO satellites are simultaneously visible to the UE, a condition not always met by realistic LEO constellations.
(iii) The existing PRS waveform does not provide sufficient frequency resolution to estimate f_i with the accuracy needed for FDOA-based 3D localization.

Problem. Design a positioning scheme — comprising (a) a modified or new downlink reference-signal waveform, (b) an associated UE measurement procedure that extracts Doppler observables with quantified frequency resolution, and (c) an estimator that fuses FDOA with available delay-based observables — such that, under realistic LEO visibility (in particular, when fewer than 8 satellites are simultaneously visible), the scheme provides consistent 3D position estimates whose error is bounded in terms of receiver SNR, integration time, ephemeris uncertainty, and constellation geometry. Quantify the trade-offs between Doppler resolution, signaling overhead, and achievable localization accuracy, and prove conditions on the satellite geometry and waveform parameters under which the joint delay+FDOA estimator is identifiable and asymptotically efficient.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open research direction for 6G NTN positioning. Standardization of Doppler/FDOA support in 5G/6G PRS is still under active discussion in 3GPP and the research literature; no published work provides a complete, standards-ready solution simultaneously addressing PRS redesign for Doppler resolution, sub-8-satellite 3D FDOA estimation, and integration with delay-based methods. Status appears open.

status_evidence.title: NTN-based 6G Localization: Vision, Role of LEOs, and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Listed among open problems: FDOA requires PRS redesign and at least 8 visible LEOs for 3D estimation.
status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly framed as an open problem in the NTN 6G localization roadmap.
